blogs.title: When One Dose Isn’t Enough: The Hidden Danger of 0.3 mg Epinephrine Auto‑Injectors
blogs.description: An in‑depth look at how sub‑optimal epinephrine dosing in adult anaphylaxis can prolong shock, fuel multiphasic reactions, and why the standard 0.5 mg dose is critical. Includes discussion of recent data, practical solutions for emergency departments, and a walk‑through of the case’s dosing pitfalls.

blogs.title: Biphasic vs. Multiphasic Anaphylaxis: What Makes the Difference?
blogs.description: Clarifies the definitions, diagnostic criteria, and clinical nuances between biphasic and multiphasic anaphylaxis. Explores why the 60‑year‑old patient’s four‐episode course was so unique, how to differentiate true relapse from residual allergen, and the current gaps in guideline recommendations.

blogs.title: Corticosteroids in Anaphylaxis: Time to Rethink the Routine?
blogs.description: Examines the shifting evidence regarding steroids in acute anaphylaxis and biphasic reactions. Presents the controversy highlighted by this case, reviews recent meta‑analyses, and offers practical guidance on when, if ever, steroids should be included in anaphylaxis protocols.

blogs.title: Systemic Mastocytosis as a Hidden Culprit in Severe Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: Explores the link between mast cell disorders and increased severity/biphasic risk in anaphylaxis. Discusses diagnostic challenges, WHO criteria, and the implications of a near‑diagnosis in the case, with tips on how to screen patients when alarm bells ring during an anaphylactic event.

blogs.title: Observation Periods After Anaphylaxis: Evidence, Practice, and the Big Gap
blogs.description: Reviews existing guideline recommendations on post‑reaction monitoring, evaluates the real‑world variability in hospital stays, and proposes a risk‑stratified approach. Uses the patient’s 24‑hour ICU observation to illustrate the practical trade‑offs between safety and resource allocation.

blogs.title: Building a Registry for Complex Anaphylaxis: Why We Need Real‑World Data
blogs.description: Advocates for a dedicated multiphasic/anaphylaxis case registry. Details what data points are most valuable, how to capture them without delaying care, and how aggregated information could drive future consensus guidelines and improve patient outcomes.
